    - **Light Theme ("Mint & Navy"):** Primary `#EAFBF3`, Panel `#FFFFFF`, Border `#CDEFE0`, Accent/Dye `#0A2540`, Ok `#059669`, Block `#DC2626`, Text `#0A2540`.
- **Navigation & Feature Restorations:**
  - Added clean text navigation for all views: `Executive Dashboard`, `Agent Monitoring`, `Threat Detection`, `Break It (Red Team)`, `Event Logs`, and `Policy & Settings`.
  - In `dashboard.py`:
    - Fixed the missing **"Run side by side"** comparison handler.
    - Integrated execution trace timelines and sandbox state inspection cards (Outbox exfiltration log, Shell command log, File mutations, and Outbound HTTP requests).
  - In `break_it.py`:
    - Updated styles to use dynamic CSS tokens so all panels, attack presets, and metrics render in both Dark and Light palettes.

#### 2. Upgrades U0–U6
- **U0 (Baseline):** Captured baseline metrics in [`baseline_results.md`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/benchmarks/results/baseline_results.md) and documented adapter mappings in [`PROGRESS.md`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/PROGRESS.md).
- **U1 (Provenance v1 & Pluggable Architecture):** Established [`provenance.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/src/firewall/provenance.py) with `using_version("v1" | "v2")`, `arg_is_trusted()`, and `path_key()`.
- **U2 (Red-Team Fuzzer & v1 Measurement):** Built the 109-case adversarial mutation suite covering families `F1`–`F7` ([`fuzz.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/src/redteam/fuzz.py)). Measured 21 bypasses on v1.
- **U3 (Provenance v2 Hardened):** Implemented NFKC normalization, zero-width stripping, strict token boundary validation, URL authority parsing, and canonical path containment. Reduced bypasses to **0 / 109 (100% neutralized)**.
- **U4 (Red-Team Measurement v2):** Generated deterministic benchmark reports comparing v1 vs v2 ([`redteam_report.md`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/benchmarks/results/redteam_report.md)).
- **U5 (Bounded Policy Verifier):** Implemented exhaustive sequence checker evaluating 2,048 state sequences ([`verify.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/src/firewall/verify.py), `verify_policy.py`).
- **U6 ("Break It" UI Lab & Final Tests):** Deployed the interactive attack lab and verified all unit and integration test suites pass.

   - Test suites continue to pass cleanly.

If you refresh the Streamlit app in your browser or run:

You will now see the graphic pipeline with the connecting pipe running left-to-right, the numbered circular step nodes, verdict tags, and the animated **BLOCKED** stamp.

## 🤖 Assistant (Response #600)
*2026-11-07T22:32:30Z*

### Why That Happened

In Markdown / CommonMark syntax, **any line that begins with 4 or more leading spaces after an empty/blank line is automatically interpreted by the Markdown parser as an indented code block (`<pre><code>`)**.

In [`app/views/dashboard.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/app/views/dashboard.py), the HTML string passed to `st.markdown(..., unsafe_allow_html=True)` was written as a triple-quoted multiline Python string with blank lines and 12-space indentation:
```python
<div class="pipe-flow"></div>

            <div class="trace-step step-active-trust">  # <-- 12 spaces after a blank line!
              <div class="node-circle">1</div>
...
```
Because of the blank line followed by 12 leading spaces, Streamlit's Markdown engine converted everything from `<div class="trace-step step-active-trust">` onwards into a literal code box with a copy icon (which is exactly what was shown in your screenshot).

---

### What Was Fixed

1. In [`app/views/dashboard.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/app/views/dashboard.py), cleaned up the `st.markdown` call so that no inner tags are indented with 4+ spaces after empty lines. The HTML is now passed cleanly so Streamlit parses it as raw DOM elements rather than a Markdown code block.
2. Verified that all styling and test suites pass cleanly.

If you refresh your Streamlit dashboard in the browser, the code snippet box will be gone and replaced by the graphic pipeline with the animated flow line, numbered circular nodes, and verdict tags.

/* Hero Trace & Animated Pipe Flow */
.trace-container {{
  background: var(--panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 2px;
  padding: 2.25rem 2rem;
  margin-bottom: 2rem;
  position: relative;
  overflow: hidden;
}}

.trace-pipe-wrapper {{
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  margin: 3rem 1.5rem 2.5rem 1.5rem;
}}

.pipe-track {{
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  height: 6px;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  z-index: 1;
  background: var(--line);
}}

.pipe-flow {{
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  height: 6px;
  transform: translateY(-50%);
  z-index: 2;
  background: linear-gradient(to right, var(--trust) 0%, var(--trust) 50%, var(--dye) 50%, var(--dye) 100%);
  background-size: 100% 100%;
  animation: pipeFill 2.2s cubic-bezier(0.6, 0, 0.2, 1) forwards;
  clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0);
}}

@keyframes pipeFill {{
  0% {{ clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0); }}
  100% {{ clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); }}
}}

.trace-step {{
  position: relative;
  z-index: 3;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  text-align: center;
  width: 200px;
}}

.node-circle {{
  width: 38px;
  height: 38px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--panel);
  border: 2px solid var(--line);
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif;
  font-size: 1.3rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  color: var(--ink);
  margin-bottom: 0.85rem;
  transition: all 0.2s ease;
}}

.step-active-trust .node-circle {{
  border-color: var(--trust);
  color: var(--trust);
}}

.step-active-dye .node-circle {{
  border-color: var(--dye);
  color: var(--dye);
}}

.step-label {{
  font-size: 11px;
  color: var(--muted);
  margin-bottom: 0.35rem;
}}

.step-tool {{
  font-family: 'Martian Mono', monospace;
  font-size: 12px;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--ink);
  margin-bottom: 0.45rem;
}}

.verdict-tag {{
  display: inline-block;
  font-family: 'Martian Mono', monospace;
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 600;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  padding: 2px 7px;
  border-radius: 2px;
}}

.tag-allow {{ color: var(--ok); }}
.tag-taint {{ color: var(--ask); }}
.tag-block {{ color: var(--dye); }}

.blocked-stamp {{
  position: absolute;
  right: 2.2rem;
  top: 1.8rem;
  font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif;
  font-size: 2.4rem;
  font-weight: 900;
  color: var(--dye);
  border: 3px solid var(--dye);
  padding: 2px 14px;
  border-radius: 2px;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  line-height: 0.95;
  transform: scale(1) rotate(-7deg);
  opacity: 1;
  animation: stampSlam 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.275) 2.2s both;
  pointer-events: none;
}}

@keyframes stampSlam {{
  0% {{
    opacity: 0;
    transform: scale(2.2) rotate(-15deg);
  }}
  100% {{
    opacity: 1;
    transform: scale(1) rotate(-7deg);
  }}
}}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {{
  .pipe-flow {{
    animation: none !important;
    clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0) !important;
  }}
  .blocked-stamp {{
    animation: none !important;
    opacity: 1 !important;
    transform: scale(1) rotate(-7deg) !important;
  }}
}}


@media (max-width: 768px) {{
  .readout-strip {{
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  }}
  .blocked-stamp {{
    position: static;
    display: inline-block;
    margin: 1rem 0;
    font-size: 2rem;
  }}
}}
</style>

## 🤖 Assistant (Response #711)
*2026-11-07T23:09:45Z*

### What Was Fixed

Based on the uploaded comparison screenshots, there were two distinct visual bugs causing the dark boxes and illegible text in Light mode:

1. **Dark Dropdown Boxes & Select Controls:**
   - Streamlit's native BaseWeb selectboxes (`div[data-baseweb="select"]`) and input containers had an unstyled dark background and dark text clash in Light mode.
   - **Fix:** Added `--input-bg`, `--input-border`, and `--input-color` CSS tokens to both Light (`#EAFBF3` mint-white with `#0A2540` deep navy text) and Dark modes.
   - Styled all dropdown menus (`div[data-baseweb="select"]`, `div[role="combobox"]`, `div[data-baseweb="popover"]`, and `ul[role="listbox"]`) so the dropdown boxes in the sidebar and scenario picker appear crisp, light, and fully legible with no dark blocks.

2. **Connecting Pipe Overlapping Step Labels:**
   - The animated connecting pipe was positioned with `top: 50%` relative to the entire step column (which includes the circle, the label, the tool name, and the tag). Because of this, the horizontal line was running straight across the middle of the text (`User prompt`, `Context tainted`, `Exfiltration blocked`).
   - **Fix:** Positioned the pipe at `top: 19px` (the exact vertical center of the 38px `.node-circle`). The colored flow line now connects smoothly through the circular nodes `(1) ——— (2) ——— (3)` with the text labels cleanly below it, matching your reference screenshot.

---

### How to Preview & Push

1. Refresh your Streamlit app in the browser (or run `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m streamlit run app/app.py`).
2. When ready, commit and push to git:
```powershell
cd C:\Users\Vani\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\agent-firewall
git add .
git commit -m "fix(ui): eliminate dark dropdown boxes in light mode and align hero pipeline behind step circles"
git push origin main
```

## 🤖 Assistant (Response #728)
*2026-11-07T23:14:59Z*

### Exactly What Happened

In your screenshot, Streamlit's sidebar had simply **collapsed to the left margin** (which Streamlit does when the browser window changes width or when the collapse chevron `«` is clicked).

However, the CSS from the UI branch previously included:
```css
header[data-testid="stHeader"] {
  display: none !important;
}
```
In modern Streamlit versions, Streamlit places the **expand/open sidebar button (`>`)** inside that top header bar. Because the entire `stHeader` was hidden with `display: none`, once the sidebar collapsed, the button to un-collapse it became invisible!

---

### The Fix Applied

1. **Restored the Header Bar & Toggle Button:**
   - Changed `header[data-testid="stHeader"]` to `background: transparent !important;` so it doesn't take up visual space or introduce ugly borders, while keeping Streamlit's internal controls active.
   - Explicitly styled `[data-testid="stSidebarCollapsedControl"]` (the expand chevron) so that whenever the sidebar is collapsed, the open arrow button (`>`) is always clearly visible at the top-left, floating above the canvas.
2. **Fixed Dark Mode & Light Mode:**
   - The toggle button automatically inherits your theme colors (`var(--panel)`, `var(--ink)`, `var(--line)`).

---

### What to Do Now

1. Refresh your browser tab.
2. In the top-left corner, click the **`>`** (chevron arrow) to immediately slide the sidebar back open.
3. You will see all 6 navigation tabs, the Light/Dark mode switcher, and the firewall settings right where they belong.

---

## 🤖 Assistant (Response #742)
*2026-11-07T23:19:42Z*

### What Was Causing the Black Highlight Boxes in Light Mode

In your screenshot, Streamlit's base widgets (`stSelectbox`) render via a nested hierarchy:
1. `[data-testid="stSelectbox"]`
2. `div[data-baseweb="select"]`
3. `div[role="combobox"]`
4. Inner `div` and `span` value containers.

Streamlit's default theme settings had a fallback dark background (`#02070A` / `#07131B`), which applied to the inner `[data-testid="stSelectbox"]` and `div[role="combobox"]` elements. As a result, even though the outer container changed, the inner box rendered as a solid black block with dark text, making `Light (Mint & Navy)`, `stage2`, `scripted`, and `[ATTACK] A01:...` almost completely unreadable.

---

### The Fix

Updated [`app/styles.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/app/styles.py) with a comprehensive style rule:
1. **Targeted Every Select Element Level:**
   - `.stSelectbox`, `[data-testid="stSelectbox"]`
   - `div[data-baseweb="select"]`, `div[role="combobox"]`
   - `div[data-baseweb="select"] > div`
2. **Eliminated Black Backgrounds & Enforced Light Colors:**
   - Applied `background-color: var(--input-bg) !important;` (`#EAFBF3` mint-white in Light mode, `#14141C` deep ink in Dark mode).
   - Applied `border-color: var(--input-border) !important;`.
   - Set all inner `span`, `p`, `div`, and SVG dropdown arrow icons to inherit `var(--input-color)` (`#0A2540` deep navy in Light mode, `#F4F4FA` in Dark mode) with `background-color: transparent !important;`.
3. **Dropdown Popovers & Options:**
   - Overrode `[data-baseweb="popover"]` and `li[role="option"]` so that when you click any dropdown, the menu items also match the light mint-and-navy theme.

---

### Next Step

Simply refresh your browser tab (or press `F5` / `Ctrl+R`). All the black boxes in the sidebar and dashboard will now be light mint-white with crisp, dark navy text.

   - Increased the animation duration from `0.3s` to **`0.55s`** with an organic exponential decelerating curve.

   - Added `transition: opacity 0.4s ease;` to the main section to blend the transition gracefully.

/* Dropdown popover menu & options list when clicked */
div[data-baseweb="popover"],
div[data-baseweb="popover"] > div,
div[data-baseweb="popover"] ul,
ul[role="listbox"],

li[role="option"] {{

ul[role="listbox"] li:hover,
ul[role="listbox"] li[aria-selected="true"],

}}

[data-testid="stRadio"] div[role="radiogroup"] {{

}}

  padding: 0.4rem 0.65rem !important;
  border-radius: 4px !important;
  transition: all 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) !important;
  margin-bottom: 2px !important;
  cursor: pointer !important;
}}

[data-testid="stRadio"] label:hover {{
  background-color: var(--panel-alt) !important;
  transform: translateX(3px) !important;
}}

[data-testid="stRadio"] label[data-checked="true"],
[data-testid="stRadio"] label:has(input:checked) {{
  background-color: var(--panel-alt) !important;
  border-left: 3px solid var(--trust) !important;
  padding-left: calc(0.65rem - 3px) !important;
}}

[data-testid="stRadio"] label,
[data-testid="stRadio"] div,
[data-testid="stRadio"] span,
[data-testid="stRadio"] p {{
  color: var(--ink) !important;
  font-family: 'Martian Mono', monospace !important;
  font-size: 12px !important;
}}

def get_theme_css(theme: str = "dark") -> str:
    """Generate dynamic CSS tokens and rules for the active theme."""
    is_dark = theme.lower() == "dark"

    if is_dark:
        bg = "#0A0A0F"
        panel = "#14141C"
        panel_alt = "#1A1A24"
        ink = "#F4F4FA"
        muted = "#9B9BB0"

## 🤖 Assistant (Response #889)
*2026-11-08T00:21:04Z*

### Silky Smooth, Slow, and Lag-Free Transitions Applied

The harshness and perceived lag when switching tabs came from two browser rendering factors:
1. **Vertical Coordinate Shifts (`transform: translateY(...)`):** Changing `translateY` on a container with heavy data tables, metric cards, and charts causes the browser to trigger continuous layout recalculations (paint reflows), making the transition feel stuttery.
2. **Animation Duration:** 0.3s–0.5s was too fast to create a calm, cinematic dissolve.

---

### The Fix

Updated [`app/styles.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/app/styles.py):

1. **Slow & Continuous Dissolve (`0.75s ease-in-out`):**
   ```css
   .block-container {
     animation: smoothFadeIn 0.75s ease-in-out forwards;
     contain: content;
   }

   @keyframes smoothFadeIn {
     0% {
       opacity: 0;
     }
     100% {
       opacity: 1;
     }
   }
   ```
2. **Eliminated All Layout Reflows (`contain: content`):**
   - Removed the vertical translation jump completely so the browser operates purely on the GPU compositor thread using alpha channels (`opacity: 0 → 1`).
   - Added `contain: content;` to isolate page rendering, guaranteeing zero lag or frame drops regardless of page complexity.
3. **Smooth Canvas Blend:**
   - Applied `transition: opacity 0.5s ease-in-out;` on `section[data-testid="stMain"]` to blend transitions seamlessly.

---

### To Test & Commit

Refresh your browser window (`Ctrl+R` / `F5`) and switch between tabs like **Executive Dashboard** and **Agent Monitoring**. The views now cross-fade smoothly and slowly without any lag.

When ready to push to your repository:
```powershell
cd C:\Users\Vani\.gemini\antigravity\scratch\agent-firewall
git add .
git commit -m "perf(ui): zero-lag 0.75s ease-in-out pure opacity cross-fade transition"
git push origin main
```

The **Deploy** button at the top-right corner is a **built-in feature of Streamlit Community Cloud**:

### 1. What It Does
- When running Streamlit locally on your machine, Streamlit automatically displays that button so developers can one-click deploy their local app to **Streamlit Community Cloud** (share.streamlit.io).
- It is only visible to you while developing/running locally.

---

### 2. Can We Hide It?
Yes! In production applications or dashboards, you typically hide the Deploy button and Streamlit's default meatball menu (`...`) so the interface looks like a dedicated, standalone software tool rather than a developer playground.

I have hidden it via CSS in [`app/styles.py`](file:///C:/Users/Vani/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/agent-firewall/app/styles.py):

```css
/* Hide default Streamlit Deploy button and developer menu */
.stAppDeployButton,
[data-testid="stAppDeployButton"],
#MainMenu,
footer {
  display: none !important;
}
```
